Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "i'm setting up the desktop uploader for the archive team and i need help checking the transfer options before i start the first batch i want the app to keep a transfer available after the network drops so please turn on this setting
transfer.allow_resume
i found it in the advanced section but i'm not sure whether it applies to queued files or only a file that's already moving please explain that distinction without changing any other setting the first batch has 24 folders and each folder has 18 files that's 24 folders not 24 files total the upload limit should stay at 12 megabytes per second and the retry count should be 4 not 5 i said five a moment ago sorry four retries leave the destination as the existing team archive and don't rename any files for the test please use one folder with 18 files and tell me which status indicator shows that the transfer resumed after a brief disconnect i don't want the uploader to delete the local copies when a transfer finishes and please keep the current sign in account as it is i can test this after lunch if the network monitor is available otherwise i will wait for the connection to settle and run it tomorrow", "output": "I'm setting up the desktop uploader for the archive team, and I need help checking the transfer options before I start the first batch. I want the app to keep a transfer available after the network drops, so please turn on this setting:
transfer.allow_resume

The first batch has 24 folders, and each folder has 18 files; that's 24 folders, not 24 files total. The upload limit should stay at 12 megabytes per second, and the retry count should be four, not five. I said five a moment ago—sorry, four retries. Please use one folder with 18 files and tell me which status indicator shows that the transfer resumed after a brief disconnect. I don't want the uploader to delete the local copies when a transfer finishes, and please keep the current sign-in account as it is. I can test this after lunch if the network monitor is available; otherwise, I will wait for the connection to settle and run it tomorrow."}]
